icps.label: The core filter (what we launch with)

fields.companySize: $1M-$10M gross revenue is the target. You'll consider $750,000+ if other standards are met, so that's our hard floor. Below $1M the engagement eats too much of the bottom line (your math: $1M x 20% margin = $200k profit, and $60k of that is already 25%+). $20M+ is possible but you called it a harder sale. High-margin businesses only.
countries: United States. Georgia first (they already know your firm), then Southeast, then East Coast, then national. You also have a Santa Monica office, so the West Coast is open later.
signals: From your own Tax Planning PDF - ideal fit is 'growing income, MULTIPLE ENTITIES, material estimated taxes, or MAJOR UPCOMING TRANSACTIONS'. Multiple entities and a pending transaction are both things we can spot from public data - that's a real targeting signal.
From your CFO PDF - 'owner-led, growing, profitable, needs financial leadership WITHOUT hiring a full-time CFO'.

fields.companySize: $2M-$20M in settlements. Contingency-fee firms: they front case costs for years and get paid in huge unpredictable lumps. That's a cash-flow problem run by litigators.
countries: United States - Atlanta is a heavy PI market

fields.companySize: $1M-$10M. NOT general dental - the median single-location practice sits at or under your floor. Specialty and cash-pay clear it easily: oral surgery, perio, ortho, plastics, med spa, dermatology, fertility, LASIK.

icps.label: Candidate: The 'PE is coming for you' cluster

fields.companySize: $2M-$10M. Specialty trades (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing - NOT general contracting), independent insurance agencies, MSPs. All in active roll-up markets. Their exit multiple depends on financials that survive diligence, and most get marked down because the books are a mess.

doNotTarget: Restaurants - for CFO or tax. They're a BOOKKEEPING campaign, separate, later. Your call.
Anything thin-margin: retail, grocery, distribution/wholesale, general contracting, staffing, trucking. Same reason as restaurants - $5M of revenue at a 5% margin can't fund a $60k engagement.
Under $750k - that's the hard floor you gave us. $750k-$1M only if the business is unusually profitable. Under that, they're bookkeeping leads and we park them for the later campaign.

Nothing is geographically banned - you have a Santa Monica office and clients all over. But you said start East Coast and venture out, because a distant prospect tends to want someone local. So: Georgia first, then outward. Not a hard exclusion.

We'd still like to TEST it as one cold variant. Cold email has zero trust and a guarantee is the strongest trust device there is. If it loses to your frame, we drop it. Your name, your call.
problemsSolved: TAX (your words): taxes only get managed when a return is due. By then the year has closed, the transactions have happened, and the strongest planning options are gone. Every year that repeats, the owner hands the government an interest-free loan.

CFO (your words): financials arrive late, reports are hard to understand, cash flow feels unpredictable, margins are unclear - and leadership is making major decisions without trusted financial guidance.
The question your prospects actually ask: 'Why does profit not match the cash in the bank?'
proof: A client doing $23M/year: $1.5M found in the first two months, before we touched their taxes. (NEED YOUR OK TO USE THIS.)

Investor-ready reporting for a personal injury firm that's recovered $100M+ in settlements.

100+ five-star Google reviews (please confirm the number you want us to claim).
offer.guidingQuestion: ANSWERED - it was in your own Tax Planning Overview. Your 5-phase process (Discovery -> Tax Exposure Analysis -> Strategy Design, where you QUANTIFY the potential impact -> Implementation -> Monitoring) is exactly how you know 2x is achievable before you accept an engagement. That's the mechanism, and it's what turns 'we'll save you money' into something a stranger can believe. It's now in the copy.
offer.frontEndOffer: Your own named CTAs, straight from your PDFs: a 'Tax Planning Review' and a 'Fractional CFO Discovery Review'. Far stronger than 'hop on a call' - it's a named thing with a defined scope. No pricing in the email, no lead magnet.
leadMagnets: NO lead magnet, NO pricing in email 1. You said prospects get intimidated by price before they understand the value - so the email's only job is to earn the Review.
HARD WALL: FP&A + dashboards are CFO-ONLY. Tax-planning copy never mentions them. (Note the reverse IS true - your CFO service includes tax planning integration.)

Your three PDFs (Tax Planning Overview, Fractional CFO Overview, Dashboards Overview) are REPLY assets, sent after someone bites - never attached to a cold email. Attachments wreck deliverability, and Dashboards is your differentiator, not a giveaway.

emails.subject: interest-free loan
emails.body:
{{first_name}} - every year a business overpays the IRS, it's handing the government an interest-free loan.

It happens because accountants FILE. They don't PLAN. By the time the return is due, the year has closed, the transactions have already happened, and the strongest options are gone.

Most of what's still open for this tax year has to be done before Dec 31, not discovered in April.

Worth a 15-minute Tax Planning Review to see what you could legally keep?

emails.subject: projected liability
emails.body:
{{first_name}} - three questions most owners can't answer until it's too late to act on them:

- What's my projected tax liability this year?
- Is my entity structure still the right one?
- Which strategies can still be implemented before Dec 31?

That's what a Tax Planning Review answers. We model your exposure and quantify what's actually recoverable before anything is agreed.

Worth 15 minutes?

emails.subject: profit vs cash
emails.body:
CFO ANGLE ONLY - dashboards and FP&A are never mentioned to a tax-planning prospect.

{{first_name}} - why doesn't profit match the cash in the bank?

It's the question we hear most from owner-led companies that have outgrown bookkeeping. Revenue is up, but the reports land late, margins are unclear, and big decisions get made without a financial read.

We run a Fractional CFO Discovery Review: reporting quality, cash-flow visibility, KPIs, and where margin is leaking. One client at $23M found $1.5M in the first two months.

Worth a look at what yours would show?

emails.subject: worth $20k to keep $30k?
emails.body:
TEST VARIANT - the guarantee as the OPENER. You'd rather hold it for a 50/50 prospect; we want to see whether it wins cold, where trust is zero. If it loses to your frame, we drop it.

{{first_name}} - if you owed the IRS $50,000, would you rather hand them $50,000, or hand us $20,000 and keep $30,000?

We run the exposure analysis and quantify the savings BEFORE we accept the engagement. That's why we can say: if the plan doesn't find at least 2x its own fee, you're fully refunded.

Worth 15 minutes?

items.a: Never ignore it - acknowledge it first, because if you ignore that, they'll assume you'd ignore them as a client. Then reframe: we're here to give you a second opinion. Does your current accounting team offer FP&A - intuitive financial dashboards that help you make informed decisions? Investor-ready reports? Your words: the conversion rate on that reframe is high.
items.ask: This is captured from the call - did we get it right?

You didn't name a vertical, and you told us to lean on our expertise. But prospects WILL ask. Do you want to be positioned as generalists who go deep on the numbers, or should we lead with a specific industry you've served? (Your PI law firm client is the strongest single story you have.)

items.a: A rarity as an objection. A firm our size, with our review count - they know we have CPAs and EAs on staff.
items.ask: Confirming so copy claims exactly what's true: we will say the FIRM has CPAs and EAs. We will not make any claim about a specific individual's licence unless you tell us to. Good?

items.a: Our costs are based on your bottom line - our number one goal is protecting it. Every business is different, so get on a call, we'll understand yours end to end, and we'll give you a live quote right there. (Your line: nine times out of ten, we close them.)
items.ask: Captured from the call. Confirm we never state a price in an email?

items.q: "Is a tax firm even allowed to email me like this?"
items.ask: You know these rules far better than we do. Anything we must say, or must never say, in an email going out under your name?

risks.risk: Lead quality in weeks 1-3 - the one that decides everything
risks.prevention: You told us quality is the whole game, so we're building the check in from day one: every interested reply gets validated against revenue and margin BEFORE it reaches your calendar. But we need your feedback fast. If a lead is wrong, we have to hear it in week one, not month two - by month two the campaign has already been tuned around the wrong signal.

risks.risk: We don't know your industry yet
risks.prevention: You told us to lean on our expertise, so we go deliberately BROAD at launch and tighten around whoever actually replies. Narrowing to a vertical before we have data would be guessing. Your 5-10 examples are what shortcut this.

Monitored daily, with warm-up buffers and rotation. Google and Microsoft change their filters every few months; when it happens it's usually a two-week dip. You'll hear it from us first, with the fix attached.

risks.risk: A cold prospect arrives colder than a referral
risks.prevention: Your pipeline has always been referral, where trust already exists. A cold prospect asks harder questions earlier. That's our job to absorb, not yours: every booked meeting arrives with a one-pager giving your closer the revenue and the pain points before they dial - exactly the pre-qualification you asked for.

expectations.greatMeeting: The decision-maker on the call (you said 9/10 they show up when money is the topic), their revenue understood before it starts, and their pain points already known - so your closer knows what to hit. Pre-qualified, ready to close, not asking beginner questions.
